articles.title: Kerala Police find similarities between Gurumurthy, Kochi synagogue arson cases; yet to find evidence of Lawrence Bishnoi links
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police in Keralam have found similarities between the case in which a Tamil Nadu native was arrested recently from Palakkad for alleged links with criminal networks and the arson attack allegedly targeting a synagogue in Ernakulam.

Initial investigations have revealed similarities in the modus operandi of 27-year-old Gurumurthy, who was arrested from Ottappalam, Palakkad, on November 12, and Ebin P. Paul, 32, who has been remanded in judicial custody since his arrest for allegedly setting fire to a plant nursery located in front of the 800-year-old Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Ernakulam on October 12, State Police Chief Ravada A. Chandrasekhar said on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Though the accused in both cases were suspected to have links with the infamous Lawrence Bishnoi gang, the police said they were yet to find evidence of any direct connection between the accused and the group.
The Thrissur police are investigating the case against Gurumurthy, while the National Investigation Agency (NIA) has taken over the probe into the arson case.

“Initial investigation revealed that Gurumurthy was taking assignments from criminal networks operating mainly through social media. He used to take photographs of various locations and send them to his handler in return for money. He was paid in cryptocurrency and using GPay. The case bears some similarities to the Ebin Paul case, in which an incendiary device was thrown at the synagogue in Kochi. We are examining whether the handler is connected to that case,” Mr. Chandrasekhar told reporters.

Another youth was arrested in Mumbai recently for alleged links with Gurumurthy. Yash Singh, 20, a native of Navi Mumbai, was arrested by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad for allegedly conducting reconnaissance of Jewish establishments, including Chabad House in Mumbai.
Mr. Singh, who was reportedly recruited by Gurumurthy, was later handed over to the Thrissur City police. He was brought to Thrissur on Sunday and remanded in judicial custody.

articles.title: Supreme Court asks Centre, States to file status reports on setting up of special courts to hear NDPS Act cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 16, 2026) asked the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to file fresh status reports on progress made in the establishment of 449 special courts to hear cases of heinous offences under the NDPS Act.

A Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana took note of the submissions of Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that not much progress has been made in pursuance of the orders passed by the apex court recently on setting up of special courts.
"This is a three-judge matter also," Justice Bagchi said and referred to the non-availability of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant for the hearing.

The Bench said that it will keep the suo motu case concerning the creation of exclusive special courts for speedy trials under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act and the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act after a few weeks and preferably before the winter vacation in December.
It asked the Centre, States and Union Territories to file fresh status reports on the progress made by them in creating special courts for early disposal of pending cases under the NIA and NDPS Acts.
Earlier, the Bench had expressed concern over the alarming increase in narcotics-related offences across the country and the growing pendency of cases under the NDPS Act.
On September 7, the court had directed the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to expedite the establishment of exclusive special courts, preferably within six weeks.
According to an affidavit filed by the Union government, 449 exclusive NDPS courts have been identified as necessary across the country to address the mounting backlog of cases.
The Centre had told the court that 176 of these courts were already operational.

Taking note of the figures, the Bench had observed that the existing pendency and the "unfortunate, alarming increase" in offences under the NDPS Act made it imperative to establish all the identified courts at the earliest.

The Bench had directed the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to ensure the necessary infrastructure and appointment of adequate staff so that the remaining courts could become operational preferably within six weeks.
Apart from NDPS cases, the Bench also reviewed the progress made by States in establishing exclusive special courts for trials under Section 11 of the NIA Act, 2008.

articles.title: Patients allege rat bites, dog roaming in Rajasthan’s Pali govt hospital ward; staff faces action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A dog roaming inside a hospital ward and complaints of patients being bitten by rats have prompted the management of a government hospital in Rajasthan's Pali to take disciplinary action against the staff for alleged negligence, officials said on Monday (November 16, 2026).

The hospital administration said that they have shifted the ward in-charge and a nursing staff member to other wards and initiated action to remove a Home Guard personnel and a helper from their duties.

The action followed complaints from patients admitted to Surgical Ward C. On Sunday (November 15), patients Moti Singh and Haseena Bano, wife of another patient, Babu Khan, alleged that rats had bitten their feet while they were sleeping in the ward at night.
A video also surfaced showing a dog roaming freely through the hospital corridors, raising questions over cleanliness and security arrangements at the government-run facility.
Hospital superintendent Dr. Kailash Parihar said he visited Surgical Ward C along with a team and interacted with patients to assess the situation.
Following the inspection, ward in-charge Tasneem Khatoon and nursing staff member Ramkesh Meena were removed from the ward and assigned duties elsewhere, he said.
A helper and a Home Guard personnel were also removed for negligence, Mr. Parihar added.

The management also placed rat poison at several locations in the ward to prevent further incidents, and a team remained engaged in improving the ward's arrangements until late Sunday (November 15) night.
Hospital deputy superintendent Dr. R. Bishnoi said pest-control activities were being carried out regularly, but the drive would be intensified if the presence of rats was confirmed in the wards.
He said the hospital administration was taking steps to ensure that rodents were not found in patient-care areas.
Mr. Bishnoi also appealed to attendants accompanying patients to maintain cleanliness and avoid leaving food items uncovered, as it could attract rats to the hospital premises.

articles.title: Andhra NCD survey finds 59.63 lakh hypertension, 48.95 lakh diabetes cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Non-Communicable Diseases 4.0 (NCD-4) survey, which began across Andhra Pradesh on September 17, 2025, has thrown up results about the prevalence of hypertension, diabetes and cancer cases among those aged 18 and above in the State.

Following the conclusion of the survey on November 10, Health and Family Welfare Commissioner K.V.N. Chakradhar Babu and State Nodal Officer for National Health Mission K. Syamala submitted the survey findings to Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
The State has a total of 59.63 lakh hypertension cases and 48.95 lakh diabetes cases. A total of 34 lakh people in the State have both hypertension and diabetes.

According to a release by the Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare, hypertension, diabetes and cancer screening was conducted among 4.2 crore people aged above 18 in the State. Of them, the survey identified 12,23,185 new hypertension cases, which is 13.93% of the population tested, and 11,58,632 new diabetes cases, 11.45% of those tested, in addition to already existing cases.

According to the release, the districts of East Godavari, NTR, West Godavari, Kakinada and Eluru districts recorded the highest numbers of hypertension cases, while East Godavari, NTR, West Godavari, YSR Kadapa and Eluru recorded the highest diabetes cases.

Among the newly identified cases, the highest number of hypertension and diabetes cases was recorded among people aged 60 and above, accounting for 47.6% of hypertension cases and 43.39% of diabetes cases.

People aged 50-59 accounted for 29.20% of the new hypertension cases and 30.16% of the new diabetes cases. The 40-49 age group accounted for 16.77% and 18.84%, those aged 30-39 for 4.86% and 5.86%, and those aged 20-29 for 1.37% and 1.54%. Even among those aged 18 and 19, 0.20% (11,827 people) had hypertension and 0.21% (10,360 people) had diabetes.
The screening also detected 3,339 cases of oral cancer, 5,832 cases of breast cancer and 3,597 cases of cervical cancer. Around 1.46 crore women were screened for breast and cervical cancer.

Medical officers examined 9.96 lakh suspected oral cancer cases identified by field-level staff. Subsequently, 23,009 people were referred to major hospitals, where 3,339 cases were confirmed as cancer.

Among women suspected of having breast cancer, 15,374 were referred by medical officers to major hospitals, where 5,832 cases were confirmed. Regarding cervical cancer, medical officers examined and referred 19,429 suspected cases to major hospitals. Of these, 3,597 cases were confirmed.
Mr. Satya Kumar Yadav said that the State government was giving the highest priority to controlling lifestyle diseases.

articles.title: Annamalai condemns use of ‘Arohara’ chant to praise Tamil Nadu CM Vijay, Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai on Monday (November 16, 2026) condemned a member of a committee under the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department for allegedly chanting ‘Arohara’ in praise of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and HR&CE Minister during the Soorasamharam festival at Tiruchendur .

In a social media post, Mr. Annamalai said Velmurugan, a member of the HR&CE Department committee, had raised ‘Arohara’ chants for the Chief Minister and the Minister during the festival. Describing the act as condemnable, Mr. Annamalai said the “sacred devotional chant,” traditionally raised by devotees in praise of Lord Murugan, should not be used to glorify political leaders.

Such an act would undermine spiritual traditions and hurt the sentiments of millions of devotees, Mr. Annamalai contended, and urged the Chief Minister to advise those concerned against using religious festivals and devotional expressions for political praise.

Separately, interacting with journalists at the Chennai airport, Mr. Annamalai welcomed the communication from the National Commission for Women to Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police calling for an inquiry and a report into allegations that the Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh (TVK) had sent “obscene messages” to the District Collector.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation surges to 12.29% in October, fuel and power prices lead rise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s wholesale price inflation accelerated to 12.29% in October 2026, compared with 11.39% in September, according to provisional data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Monday. The All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for all commodities rose to 113.3 in October, from 112.5 in the previous month.

Fuel and power prices remained the biggest driver of wholesale inflation, with the category recording an annual inflation rate of 32.84% in October, sharply higher than the 25.85% recorded in September. Inflation in primary articles also increased to 9.24% from 8.67% during the same period. Meanwhile, inflation in manufactured products eased marginally to 9.54%, compared with 9.76% in September.

Within the fuel and power category, inflation in mineral oils rose to 45.57% in October from 40.02% in September. Crude petroleum and natural gas recorded a sharp increase, with inflation climbing to 70.80% from 57.32%. Electricity inflation also moved into positive territory at 8.06%, compared with -0.43% in the previous month.

The government’s data identified mineral oils, crude petroleum and natural gas, electricity, food articles, basic metals, chemicals, food products, non-food articles, textiles, and rubber and plastic products among the major contributors to wholesale price inflation during October.

The Wholesale Price Index’s food index, which accounts for 24.99% of the overall basket, recorded inflation of 8.58% in October, marginally lower than the 8.66% reported in September. Inflation in food articles under the primary articles category, however, rose to 8.26% from 8.14%.

Among manufactured products, inflation in chemicals and chemical products increased to 17.53% in October from 16.74% in September. Basic metals inflation rose to 17.21% from 16.96%, while textiles recorded inflation of 13.67%, compared with 13.85% in the previous month. Inflation in rubber and plastic products also increased to 13.90% from 13.47%.

The Ministry said the October WPI figures are provisional and have been compiled with a weighted response rate of 81.1%. The final WPI inflation rate for August 2026 remained unchanged at 9.92%, with the index at 110.8.
The government is scheduled to release the provisional Wholesale Price Index, Output Producer Price Index and trial Input Producer Price Index for November 2026 on December 14.

articles.title: Equity vs bonds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Diversification may have its virtues but so does concentrated investments. Sector funds are examples of concentrated bets. In this article, we draw a distinction between concentrated bets in the equity and the bond markets and show why the former is meaningful and the latter, somewhat risky.

In theory, equity has unlimited upside potential. That means stock prices can rise to any level. In the real world, stock prices have high, not unlimited, upside potential given our finite investment horizon. Yet, concentrated bets can be meaningful. If you expect the banking sector to do well in the coming year, buying units of a banking sector ETF or a sector fund could be optimal. But the downside can be high if your bet turns wrong.

articles.title: Mahanagar Gas hikes CNG prices in Mumbai by ₹1.5/kg, sixth hike since May
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Amid rising costs of input gas, Mahanagar Gas Ltd (MGL) increased prices of compressed natural gas (CNG) at their retail outlets ₹1.5 per kg.
Effective November 15, CNG in Mumbai would be priced at ₹91.5 per kg in Mumbai.
Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14.
Moreover, the latest is the second hike in the ongoing month.

The uncertainty in West Asia and the loss of supplies from Qatar, which is the world’s largest LNG producer and among the most reliable suppliers, have obligated purchasers to further alternate scouting of the natural gas and increasingly buy at spot.

In a statement, MGL said, “The ongoing Middle East crisis, coupled with reduced domestic gas allocation and increased dependence on higher-cost imported RLNG linked to international benchmarks, has significantly increased MGL’s gas procurement costs, particularly for the CNG segment, driven by strong demand and a higher share of imported gas in its input mix.”

articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, the highest-grade variety of iron ore.

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

However, in its November 4 order, the Supreme Court concurred with the need for optimum utilisation of mineral resources but left the decision on transferring mining rights to the State government’s discretion, rather than making it mandatory.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.
One of the key areas of diversification has been the African continent, with exports to that region growing 44% in April-September 2026 to $31.4 billion.
Notably, India’s trade with West Asia is recovering as countries find alternate routes and ports other than those along the constrained Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Ex-Bangladesh PM Hasina says if death is the price to pay for returning home, she is ready to face it
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, sentenced to capital punishment after she was toppled in 2024, told AFP on Monday (November 16, 2026) she would return home in December despite “the threat of death”.
Ms. Hasina fled to India in August 2024 after a student-led uprising ended her iron-fisted 15-year rule, and has remained in hiding ever since.
She was sentenced to death in absentia last year after a Bangladeshi court convicted her of crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on protesters.
“I am fully aware of the risks I face if I return,” she told AFP in an email interview.
“But I have made my decision, and no threat of death will keep me away from my own country.”

Her insistence on going back comes days after Bangladesh said she would face execution if she returned, adding that she has no further legal recourse after missing the deadline to appeal against her conviction.
The 79-year-old has repeatedly rejected the legitimacy of the trial.
Dhaka has sought her extradition from India, which says the request is under legal review.

“For months, they have demanded my return. Yet now that I am taking practical steps to come home, they appear to be more interested in threatening me... than actually allowing it to happen,” she said.
“Frankly, I find these contradictory statements from the Bangladeshi authorities rather revealing.”

Analysts suggest her promise to return is an attempt to remain politically relevant, retain the loyalty of supporters and keep alive a party that once dominated Bangladesh but whose activities are now banned.
She may also be counting on the possibility that the government would find it difficult to execute the daughter of Bangladesh’s founding leader, despite her death sentence.

articles.title: European Union nations to unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Five European Union countries including Germany and Denmark are set to announce Monday (November 16, 2026) a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda, the first such facility outside the bloc.

The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a so-called "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the EU cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules.
The five have kept the location under wraps as they negotiated with potential hosts, but European diplomats and other people briefed on the talks have indicated Rwanda as the chosen country.
The African Great Lakes nation had confirmed in August it had begun "preliminary discussions" with several European States.
And it is sending a delegation to a migration conference in Vienna, where several sources said the agreement would be unveiled at a press conference on Monday (November 16, 2026).
"We shall see next week in Vienna," Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker told reporters Friday (November 13, 2026), when asked about the matter.
The announcement is to mark the culmination of an EU push to boost deportations launched in 2024, on the back of a souring of public opinion on migration.
Migrant arrivals have steadily declined over the past three years, as the bloc struck deals to stem departures with a host of countries in Africa and West Asia.

articles.title: In reversal, U.S. to fund UN military support in Somalia for another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The United States will renew support to international military operations in Somalia, the State Department told AFP on Sunday (November 15, 2026), reversing cuts that had threatened the survival of a coalition fighting Islamist insurgents in the country.

Washington had stopped funding the United Nations Support Office for Somalia (UNSOS) — which provides crucial logistics to African Union military operations — and had given it until the end of 2027 to shut down entirely.

The Al-Qaeda-linked Al-Shabaab has been fighting the Somali government for two decades and continues to control large swathes of central Somalia despite the African Union military campaign, which was unlikely to be able to continue without UNSOS support.
Washington had expressed frustration with the Somali government's lack of progress against Al-Shabaab and the persistent political chaos in the country as reasons for cutting the funding.

But on Sunday (November 15, 2026), the U.S. State Department said that after consideration, the United States has decided to "support a one-year renewal of the mandates" for both UNSOS and the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM).
A foreign diplomatic source working on Somalia told AFP the return of US support was welcome but that the sudden swings in policy were "madness".

The source, who requested anonymity as they were not authorised to speak publicly on the matter, expressed shock that Washington did not use the promise of renewed funding to put pressure on the Somali government, which has lately descended into fresh in-fighting and political chaos that are undermining the campaign against the insurgents.

Last week, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud fired the chief justice of the Supreme Court as it was about to rule against the extension of his term in office, which it said was illegal, and which has triggered violent clashes with Opposition parties and regional leaders.
Mohamud has tried to move Somalia towards fully democratic elections, but sparked uproar when he pushed through constitutional changes in March that gave him an extra year in office.

The group claimed last month it had killed hundreds of elite Somali soldiers in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region -- potentially one of its deadliest attacks in years, although the government has not released a death toll.
Days later, Uganda, which provides the largest contingent of troops to the international military mission, said it would withdraw all its forces by the end of next year.
The United States has provided nearly $2 billion to UN missions in Somalia since 2007, and more than $1.6 billion for African troops deployed in Somalia.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Britain’s Prince William and Princess Catherine (Kate) has arrived in Mumbai for a three-day visit to India as part of the sixth edition of The Earthshot Prize. They will join 5,000 guests, including environmental innovators, business leaders, philanthropists and celebrities from across the world in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) to celebrate the prestigious environmental awards.

This marks the royal couples’ first joint overseas engagement since Ms. Kate announced her cancer diagnosis in 2024, also her first Earthshot Prize since 2022, when the ceremony was held in Boston, United States.
The couple’s return to India comes nearly a decade after their previous joint visit to the country in 2016, when they also travelled to Bhutan.
The Earthshot Prize is a prestigious environmental award, a project that was launched by Prince William in 2020, and is supported by a global coalition of philanthropists and organisations.

It aims to encourage innovative solutions to climate change and other major environmental challenges such as air pollution, waste, ocean conservation and the loss of biodiversity. It also aims to recognise 50 winners over a 10-year period.

Every year, five winners are selected from 15 global finalists, with each winner receiving £1 million (approx. ₹12.5 crore) to encourage their work and turn bold environmental ideas into actual impact. In November 2026, the sixth edition of the award arrives in Mumbai, also the first time the ceremony is held in India.

The Earthshot Awards operate on the belief that human ingenuity, innovation and optimism can help repair the planet. Each year, 15 climate solutions are shortlisted across five categories known as Earthshots: Protect and Restore Nature, Clean Our Air, Revive Our Ocean, Build a Waste Free World, and Fix Our Climate.

Under the ‘Protect and Restore Nature’ category, Bhutan’s Princess Chimi Yangzom Wangchuck and Karma Tenzin, senior forestry officer, have been shortlisted for their work in protecting the Himalayan forests which help the water systems that sustain 1.6 billion people downstream across South Asia.

Sam Murray, CEO of ‘The Indigenous Alliance’, has been shortlisted for supporting rangers caring for 270 million hectares of Australian desert. Dr Jodi Hilty, president and chief scientist, and Chief Harlan Schilling of the Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative have been shortlisted for reconnecting 3,400 km of wilderness across Canada and the United States.
Under the ‘Clean Our Air’ category, Suman Mishra, managing director and CEO of Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, has been shortlisted for building affordable electric rickshaws.

Franco Rodríguez Viau, CEO and co-founder of Satellites on Fire (Argentina), has been shortlisted for using weather forecasts, cameras and satellite technology to protect 92 million hectares across 21 countries from wildfires.
Prof Engineer Bainomugisha, founder and lead of AirQo (Uganda), has been shortlisted for building affordable air-pollution monitors for African countries.

The two countries have decided to set up a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) or Free Trade Agreement (FTA) to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries.

articles.title: India, U.S., eight other nations sign declaration to safeguard AI supply chains
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: India, the U.S. and eight other countries have signed a declaration to treat safeguarding Artificial Intelligence (AI) supply chains as a “shared endeavour” amid growing competition with China in emerging technology.

The San Francisco Declaration was signed at a meeting of the founders of the U.S.-led Pax Silica initiative convened by U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
The declaration was released by the Governments of the U.S., Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom.

The Pax Silica initiative was announced by the U.S. in December last year to secure supply chains for silicon and other minerals essential to semiconductor production and, by extension, to artificial intelligence and other advanced technological industries.

The declaration on Sunday (November 15) affirms that economic security is fundamental to national security, sets out the participants’ common understanding of the sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure that underpin Super Intelligence supply chains, and declares that safeguarding them is a shared endeavour, a State Department statement said.
The U.S. government refers to Artificial Intelligence (AI) as Super Intelligence (SI) after President Donald Trump signed an executive order to rename it.
The Declaration on Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity also resolves to establish working groups to carry common purpose into common practice.

It proposed to set up five groups covering pro-innovation policy frameworks, SI adoption in key sectors, supply chain cooperation across the SI stack, safe harbours and supply chain security hubs, and SI security and resilience.
“No nation can secure the foundations of the SI era alone, and the prosperity SI makes possible will only be as durable as the supply chains and infrastructure beneath it,” the statement said.

The declaration said that by agreeing on what must be protected and committing to protect it together, participants are laying the secure foundations on which partner nations can innovate, invest, and grow.

“Less than a year after its launch, Pax Silica is entering a new phase. With the San Francisco Declaration, the coalition cements its shared principles into a working partnership with a common baseline and a path to act on it, the statement said.

articles.title: Keralam’s orchids endure from highway trees to salt-sprayed shores
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: With their dazzling colours and ambrosial aromas, orchids are one of earth’s most distinctive flowering plant families.
They are found on every continent except Antarctica and count over 29,500 native species worldwide.
According to Orchids of India: A Pictorial Guide (2019), published by the Botanical Survey of India, Keralam accounts for more than a third of the 307 endemic orchids reported from India.
The State’s native orchid density is comparable to South American countries like Costa Rica, Viswambharan Sarasan, a research leader at the Royal Botanic Gardens in the U.K., said.
But habitat loss and fragmentation are increasingly threatening the State’s orchid diversity.
“As a child, I saw these orchids on coconut palms in our backyard [in Keralam],” he said. “But now they are disappearing from everywhere.”
However, according to Dr. Sarasan, relocating orchids from development sites or disturbed areas can reduce these losses.

Over the last three years, under Dr. Sarasan’s leadership, a research team at the KSCSTE-Malabar Botanical Garden and Institute for Plant Sciences in Calicut has rescued more than 27,000 native orchids growing on trees from being destroyed in road-widening activities in the State.

“I went to Kerala six, seven years ago, pitching this idea of growing orchids in large hubs where people congregate, such as the Napier Museum or the Kanakakunnu Palace in Thiruvananthapuram,” Dr. Sarasan, who hails from the capital city of Keralam, said.

With funding from the Royal Society International Exchanges programme, the project aimed to collect orchids from Keralam’s forests and rural areas. “However, we quickly realised there isn’t much diversity in the south,” he said.

Under the guidance of N.S. Pradeep, the scientist-in-charge at the Malabar Botanical Garden and Institute for Plant Sciences, the project shifted its focus to the northern districts of Wayanad and Kozhikode and targeted plants at risk of eradication.
Dr. Pradeep cited national and State highway projects, such as NH66 and SH59, as examples where the government felled old trees across Keralam.

articles.title: A disease rooted in social and economic vulnerability can only be eliminated as underlying systems become stronger: Dhun Davar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: India’s tuberculosis (TB) burden remains substantial despite progress. The country has the largest TB burden in the world, accounting for approximately one-quarter of all TB cases globally. The number of new cases fell 21% between 2015 and 2024, while treatment coverage rose to 92%, according to World Health Organisation data cited by the government. The Central government recently started the JOSH campaign -- launched in 11 States and 55 districts to promote screening, early diagnosis and treatment adherence. JOSH stands for Joint Squad for Health. It is a youth-led community mobilisation initiative to strengthen India’s campaign to eliminate TB.

Dhun Davar, deputy CEO & chief of programmes, AVPN, spoke to The Hindu about the challenges in the TB elimination programme. AVPN is a pan-Asian network of social investors, philanthropists, foundations, corporations and other organisations that work to direct funding and expertise towards social and environmental challenges. Its work includes health equity, gender equality, climate action and economic inclusion.

articles.title: Respiratory illnesses rise in Gaza with worst to come as winter floods arrive, WHO says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: ​The World Health Organisation warned on Friday (November 13, 2026) of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza, with worse expected after ‌heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians.

“The numbers ​already show the pressure. Acute respiratory infections are 33,000 cases higher than at ⁠the same time last year,” Dr. Reinhilde Van De Weerdt, WHO representative in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, told reporters in Geneva from Jerusalem.

Poor living conditions and severe overcrowding are driving up infections as Gaza’s population ‌is squeezed into an ever-smaller area, WHO said. The crunch has worsened as the Israeli military expands its control by advancing the “Yellow Line” — a demarcation established under ‌October’s U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
“That means people are living in more crowded conditions, where of course ‌the ⁠spread between humans of a virus is much more prone to spread,” Ms. Van ⁠De Weerdt explained.

The Israeli military told Reuters the Yellow Line aims to protect Israeli civilians and army troops from threats and that adjustments to its location follow the ceasefire agreement and international law, and are not intended ​to harm the civilian population.
“The IDF categorically ‌rejects the claim that it operates to deliberately reduce the area available to the civilian population in the Gaza Strip.”

COGAT, the Israeli military agency that coordinates aid, said that more than 93,000 tents and over 8,600 trucks carrying tarpaulin sheets, blankets and winter clothing ‌have entered Gaza since the Board of Peace, UN agencies and NGOs launched ​the winterisation plan. Equipment intended for the reconstruction of Gaza will be permitted to enter only after Hamas has been fully disarmed, it added.
Last week ⁠COGAT said that it had stepped up efforts to improve sanitary conditions before the heavy rain, in coordination with international organisations.
Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher.
“It is shocking that just a few days of rain really showed us what the coming months will bring. And winter has not even fully set in. The worst really is yet to come,” Ms. Van De Weerdt said.
Nearly a million displaced people in Gaza live in flood-exposed areas, and 400,000 of them are in locations that are considered at extremely high risk, according to ‌the WHO.

The agency said flooding heightened the risk of contaminated water, while standing water gave mosquitoes and ​pests more places to breed. Dampness encouraged mould and bacteria that are major drivers of respiratory infections, especially in young children, it said.

articles.title: India’s health spending triples to ₹4.14 lakh crore, but out-of-pocket share drops to 42.7%: NHA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Union government’s health expenditure more than tripled to ₹4.14 lakh crore in 2023-24, from ₹1.30 lakh crore in 2013-14, according to the latest National Health Accounts (NHA) estimates released by the Health Ministry.

The estimates also showed the share of out-of-pocket spending by households dropped by 21.5 percentage points over the same period, highlighting a significant transformation in the country’s healthcare financing.
As a share of total health expenditure, out-of-pocket spending fell from 64.2% in 2013-14 to 42.7% in 2023-24.

“The simultaneous increase in public healthcare financing and decline in the proportion of spending borne directly by households reflect India’s progress towards a more accessible, affordable, and financially protective healthcare system,” the Ministry said in a statement. It said out-of-pocket expenditure declined from 43.4% in 2022-23 to 42.7% in 2023-24.

“The sustained downward trend reflects the expanding role of government-supported healthcare services and financial protection mechanisms. Initiatives aimed at improving access to free and affordable treatment, medicines, diagnostics and hospital services are supporting efforts to reduce dependence on direct household spending,” it said.

The government’s share in total health expenditure increased by 14.9 percentage points over the decade, the estimates showed, while per capita government health expenditure rose from ₹1,042 in 2013-14 to ₹2,959 in 2023-24, an increase of nearly three times. Social security expenditure on health rose from 6% of total health expenditure in 2013-14 to 11% in 2023-24.

This includes government-financed health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, State insurance schemes, social health insurance, and medical expenditure for government employees. Private health insurance expenditure grew even faster, with its share rising from 3.4% to 10.2% over the decade.
The government’s expenditure on primary healthcare stood at about ₹1.53 lakh crore in 2023-24, underscoring the increased focus on primary and community-level healthcare, the Ministry said.

Initiatives such as Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, free drugs and diagnostics, the Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme, the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana and AMRIT pharmacies had contributed to efforts to improve access to affordable healthcare, it said.
The Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY had also strengthened financial protection by providing cashless hospitalisation benefits to eligible beneficiaries, it added.

The NHA Estimates for India 2023-24 are the 11th round of estimates prepared by the NHA3 Technical Secretariat, which operates within the National Health Systems Resource Centre of the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. They are prepared using the internationally recognised System of Health Accounts 2011 framework.

articles.title: Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: In the Hawaiian language, Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua means “two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe”. It is a nickname astronomers have given to a strange new discovery: an unusual pair of quasars that are also closer to each other than thought possible.

A quasar is the extremely bright centre of a galaxy, where a black hole is drawing in and heating up gases, causing them to emit radiation. The pair is unusual because it existed when the universe was only 900 million years old.

The official designation of Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua is J1602+4228AB. Astronomers first spotted the brighter of the pair in 2004, and later the James Webb Space Telescope discovered the second one nearby. Finally, scientists used the Gemini North telescope in Hawaii to study both quasars together.
The quasars are separated by only 18,100 light-years, which is extremely tight for powerful objects of this nature.

Today, astronomers around the world are struggling to explain how black holes could have grown so large within the first billion years of the universe. The black hole in one of the quasars weighs a whopping 1.5 billion solar masses. One hypothesis is that young galaxies merged and funnelled copious amounts of gases towards their central black holes, feeding their growth.

Another is that the gravity of a galaxy lying between the earth and a quasar could bend the quasar’s light, making one object appear as two. This possibility remains to be eliminated — or confirmed — as astronomers continue studying Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.

articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: Brace for impact: On rising inflation and external factors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment.

Further, there is strong evidence to suggest that the official inflation metrics are not capturing the full extent of rising prices. Data on cash with the public and UPI transactions show the value of both has been growing in double digits over the last year and more, significantly outpacing nominal GDP growth. This either suggests that the informal economy is far larger than earlier thought or, more likely, that inflation is well above what the official figures are being able to capture. Unfortunately, there are no real magic-wand fixes to this situation. Inflation is largely beyond the government’s control, and wage growth cannot happen overnight. The only way forward is to continue trying to spur sector-specific growth and warn people of the impending storm.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

fullParagraphs: The police in Keralam have found similarities between the case in which a Tamil Nadu native was arrested recently from Palakkad for alleged links with criminal networks and the arson attack allegedly targeting a synagogue in Ernakulam.

Initial investigations have revealed similarities in the modus operandi of 27-year-old Gurumurthy, who was arrested from Ottappalam, Palakkad, on November 12, and Ebin P. Paul, 32, who has been remanded in judicial custody since his arrest for allegedly setting fire to a plant nursery located in front of the 800-year-old Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Ernakulam on October 12, State Police Chief Ravada A. Chandrasekhar said on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Though the accused in both cases were suspected to have links with the infamous Lawrence Bishnoi gang, the police said they were yet to find evidence of any direct connection between the accused and the group.
The Thrissur police are investigating the case against Gurumurthy, while the National Investigation Agency (NIA) has taken over the probe into the arson case.

“Initial investigation revealed that Gurumurthy was taking assignments from criminal networks operating mainly through social media. He used to take photographs of various locations and send them to his handler in return for money. He was paid in cryptocurrency and using GPay. The case bears some similarities to the Ebin Paul case, in which an incendiary device was thrown at the synagogue in Kochi. We are examining whether the handler is connected to that case,” Mr. Chandrasekhar told reporters.

Another youth was arrested in Mumbai recently for alleged links with Gurumurthy. Yash Singh, 20, a native of Navi Mumbai, was arrested by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad for allegedly conducting reconnaissance of Jewish establishments, including Chabad House in Mumbai.
Mr. Singh, who was reportedly recruited by Gurumurthy, was later handed over to the Thrissur City police. He was brought to Thrissur on Sunday and remanded in judicial custody.

articles.title: Supreme Court asks Centre, States to file status reports on setting up of special courts to hear NDPS Act cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 16, 2026) asked the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to file fresh status reports on progress made in the establishment of 449 special courts to hear cases of heinous offences under the NDPS Act.

A Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana took note of the submissions of Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that not much progress has been made in pursuance of the orders passed by the apex court recently on setting up of special courts.
"This is a three-judge matter also," Justice Bagchi said and referred to the non-availability of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant for the hearing.

The Bench said that it will keep the suo motu case concerning the creation of exclusive special courts for speedy trials under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act and the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act after a few weeks and preferably before the winter vacation in December.
It asked the Centre, States and Union Territories to file fresh status reports on the progress made by them in creating special courts for early disposal of pending cases under the NIA and NDPS Acts.
Earlier, the Bench had expressed concern over the alarming increase in narcotics-related offences across the country and the growing pendency of cases under the NDPS Act.
On September 7, the court had directed the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to expedite the establishment of exclusive special courts, preferably within six weeks.
According to an affidavit filed by the Union government, 449 exclusive NDPS courts have been identified as necessary across the country to address the mounting backlog of cases.
The Centre had told the court that 176 of these courts were already operational.

Taking note of the figures, the Bench had observed that the existing pendency and the "unfortunate, alarming increase" in offences under the NDPS Act made it imperative to establish all the identified courts at the earliest.

The Bench had directed the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to ensure the necessary infrastructure and appointment of adequate staff so that the remaining courts could become operational preferably within six weeks.
Apart from NDPS cases, the Bench also reviewed the progress made by States in establishing exclusive special courts for trials under Section 11 of the NIA Act, 2008.

articles.title: Patients allege rat bites, dog roaming in Rajasthan’s Pali govt hospital ward; staff faces action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A dog roaming inside a hospital ward and complaints of patients being bitten by rats have prompted the management of a government hospital in Rajasthan's Pali to take disciplinary action against the staff for alleged negligence, officials said on Monday (November 16, 2026).

The hospital administration said that they have shifted the ward in-charge and a nursing staff member to other wards and initiated action to remove a Home Guard personnel and a helper from their duties.

The action followed complaints from patients admitted to Surgical Ward C. On Sunday (November 15), patients Moti Singh and Haseena Bano, wife of another patient, Babu Khan, alleged that rats had bitten their feet while they were sleeping in the ward at night.
A video also surfaced showing a dog roaming freely through the hospital corridors, raising questions over cleanliness and security arrangements at the government-run facility.
Hospital superintendent Dr. Kailash Parihar said he visited Surgical Ward C along with a team and interacted with patients to assess the situation.
Following the inspection, ward in-charge Tasneem Khatoon and nursing staff member Ramkesh Meena were removed from the ward and assigned duties elsewhere, he said.
A helper and a Home Guard personnel were also removed for negligence, Mr. Parihar added.

The management also placed rat poison at several locations in the ward to prevent further incidents, and a team remained engaged in improving the ward's arrangements until late Sunday (November 15) night.
Hospital deputy superintendent Dr. R. Bishnoi said pest-control activities were being carried out regularly, but the drive would be intensified if the presence of rats was confirmed in the wards.
He said the hospital administration was taking steps to ensure that rodents were not found in patient-care areas.
Mr. Bishnoi also appealed to attendants accompanying patients to maintain cleanliness and avoid leaving food items uncovered, as it could attract rats to the hospital premises.

articles.title: Andhra NCD survey finds 59.63 lakh hypertension, 48.95 lakh diabetes cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Non-Communicable Diseases 4.0 (NCD-4) survey, which began across Andhra Pradesh on September 17, 2025, has thrown up results about the prevalence of hypertension, diabetes and cancer cases among those aged 18 and above in the State.

Following the conclusion of the survey on November 10, Health and Family Welfare Commissioner K.V.N. Chakradhar Babu and State Nodal Officer for National Health Mission K. Syamala submitted the survey findings to Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
The State has a total of 59.63 lakh hypertension cases and 48.95 lakh diabetes cases. A total of 34 lakh people in the State have both hypertension and diabetes.

According to a release by the Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare, hypertension, diabetes and cancer screening was conducted among 4.2 crore people aged above 18 in the State. Of them, the survey identified 12,23,185 new hypertension cases, which is 13.93% of the population tested, and 11,58,632 new diabetes cases, 11.45% of those tested, in addition to already existing cases.

According to the release, the districts of East Godavari, NTR, West Godavari, Kakinada and Eluru districts recorded the highest numbers of hypertension cases, while East Godavari, NTR, West Godavari, YSR Kadapa and Eluru recorded the highest diabetes cases.

Among the newly identified cases, the highest number of hypertension and diabetes cases was recorded among people aged 60 and above, accounting for 47.6% of hypertension cases and 43.39% of diabetes cases.

People aged 50-59 accounted for 29.20% of the new hypertension cases and 30.16% of the new diabetes cases. The 40-49 age group accounted for 16.77% and 18.84%, those aged 30-39 for 4.86% and 5.86%, and those aged 20-29 for 1.37% and 1.54%. Even among those aged 18 and 19, 0.20% (11,827 people) had hypertension and 0.21% (10,360 people) had diabetes.
The screening also detected 3,339 cases of oral cancer, 5,832 cases of breast cancer and 3,597 cases of cervical cancer. Around 1.46 crore women were screened for breast and cervical cancer.

Medical officers examined 9.96 lakh suspected oral cancer cases identified by field-level staff. Subsequently, 23,009 people were referred to major hospitals, where 3,339 cases were confirmed as cancer.

Among women suspected of having breast cancer, 15,374 were referred by medical officers to major hospitals, where 5,832 cases were confirmed. Regarding cervical cancer, medical officers examined and referred 19,429 suspected cases to major hospitals. Of these, 3,597 cases were confirmed.
Mr. Satya Kumar Yadav said that the State government was giving the highest priority to controlling lifestyle diseases.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation surges to 12.29% in October, fuel and power prices lead rise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s wholesale price inflation accelerated to 12.29% in October 2026, compared with 11.39% in September, according to provisional data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Monday. The All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for all commodities rose to 113.3 in October, from 112.5 in the previous month.

Fuel and power prices remained the biggest driver of wholesale inflation, with the category recording an annual inflation rate of 32.84% in October, sharply higher than the 25.85% recorded in September. Inflation in primary articles also increased to 9.24% from 8.67% during the same period. Meanwhile, inflation in manufactured products eased marginally to 9.54%, compared with 9.76% in September.

Within the fuel and power category, inflation in mineral oils rose to 45.57% in October from 40.02% in September. Crude petroleum and natural gas recorded a sharp increase, with inflation climbing to 70.80% from 57.32%. Electricity inflation also moved into positive territory at 8.06%, compared with -0.43% in the previous month.

The government’s data identified mineral oils, crude petroleum and natural gas, electricity, food articles, basic metals, chemicals, food products, non-food articles, textiles, and rubber and plastic products among the major contributors to wholesale price inflation during October.

The Wholesale Price Index’s food index, which accounts for 24.99% of the overall basket, recorded inflation of 8.58% in October, marginally lower than the 8.66% reported in September. Inflation in food articles under the primary articles category, however, rose to 8.26% from 8.14%.

Among manufactured products, inflation in chemicals and chemical products increased to 17.53% in October from 16.74% in September. Basic metals inflation rose to 17.21% from 16.96%, while textiles recorded inflation of 13.67%, compared with 13.85% in the previous month. Inflation in rubber and plastic products also increased to 13.90% from 13.47%.

The Ministry said the October WPI figures are provisional and have been compiled with a weighted response rate of 81.1%. The final WPI inflation rate for August 2026 remained unchanged at 9.92%, with the index at 110.8.
The government is scheduled to release the provisional Wholesale Price Index, Output Producer Price Index and trial Input Producer Price Index for November 2026 on December 14.

articles.title: Equity vs bonds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Diversification may have its virtues but so does concentrated investments. Sector funds are examples of concentrated bets. In this article, we draw a distinction between concentrated bets in the equity and the bond markets and show why the former is meaningful and the latter, somewhat risky.

In theory, equity has unlimited upside potential. That means stock prices can rise to any level. In the real world, stock prices have high, not unlimited, upside potential given our finite investment horizon. Yet, concentrated bets can be meaningful. If you expect the banking sector to do well in the coming year, buying units of a banking sector ETF or a sector fund could be optimal. But the downside can be high if your bet turns wrong.

articles.title: Mahanagar Gas hikes CNG prices in Mumbai by ₹1.5/kg, sixth hike since May
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Amid rising costs of input gas, Mahanagar Gas Ltd (MGL) increased prices of compressed natural gas (CNG) at their retail outlets ₹1.5 per kg.
Effective November 15, CNG in Mumbai would be priced at ₹91.5 per kg in Mumbai.
Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14.
Moreover, the latest is the second hike in the ongoing month.

The uncertainty in West Asia and the loss of supplies from Qatar, which is the world’s largest LNG producer and among the most reliable suppliers, have obligated purchasers to further alternate scouting of the natural gas and increasingly buy at spot.

In a statement, MGL said, “The ongoing Middle East crisis, coupled with reduced domestic gas allocation and increased dependence on higher-cost imported RLNG linked to international benchmarks, has significantly increased MGL’s gas procurement costs, particularly for the CNG segment, driven by strong demand and a higher share of imported gas in its input mix.”
